name: Mode of Delivery — Rescue the Frontline Leadership Blend at Travessia
description: A four-round, intermediate corporate-learning simulation set inside Travessia Soluções Educacionais, the educational-solutions delivery unit of a major Brazilian business school in Belo Horizonte (BRL 58M delivery revenue, 28% operating margin, 34 designers/producers/engagement specialists). Travessia is measured not on enrolment but on completion and learning effectiveness — and it has a flagship in crisis. Its 16-week 'Frontline Leadership' program for Logística Pampulha S.A. reaches 1,200 dispersed, shift-based supervisors across 9 sites; built at 80% self-paced asynchronous to control cost, it is failing: only 31% on-track completion against a 75% contractual target, satisfaction 3.1/5, and the client's CHRO — about to decide a BRL 9M enterprise renewal (≈16% of revenue) — has called an emergency review. Playing the Educational Solutions Director with a hard BRL 2.4M budget ceiling (~BRL 2,000/learner) and modality cost spreads of ~BRL 8/learner-hour async, ~BRL 35 live-online, ~BRL 120 in-person, you (1) diagnose the drop-off as an objective–modality mismatch and an engagement gap, not learner motivation; (2) match each learning objective to its right modality — knowledge and compliance stay async, skill rehearsal and behaviour change move to synchronous or social formats — without over-correcting to all-live; (3) sequence the blend (flipped: async pre-work feeding live practice), engineer engagement and accountability (cohorts scheduled around rotating shifts, manager check-ins, nudges, protected time), and stay inside the ceiling; and (4) handle Round-4 curveballs — a conditional BRL 300k that pays only if completion hits 70%, a lost facilitator, and shift-clash pushback — then pitch the CHRO on completion lift, learning effectiveness, engagement design, and cost per outcome, not cost per seat. The math rewards Sagot's portfolio-of-modalities discipline and the flipped model, and punishes the five classic errors — learner-blaming, modality-by-cost, all-live overcorrection that blows the BRL 2.4M ceiling and loses scalability, accountability-free design, and a cost-per-seat pitch. Final KPIs track Projected Completion %, Learning Effectiveness, Engagement & Accountability, and Cost per Completing Learner against the budget ceiling.

Don't blame the supervisors — the live cohorts hit 82% with the same people. Async wasn't wrong for everything; it was wrong for the skill and behaviour modules, and the schedule ignored rotating shifts. Match each objective to the modality that fits it, sequence async to feed live practice, build the accountability the solitary design lacked, and stay inside R$2,4M.
